text: A random forest can be accurate, but a hundred trees can't be read like a single checklist. Stakeholders still ask the natural question — what is the model actually paying attention to? Feature importance answers it by ranking the inputs by how much the model relies on them. Done carelessly, it misleads, so this lesson also covers the traps.

Every split in every tree reduces impurity a little. A feature's impurity-based importance is the total reduction it produced across all trees, normalized so everything adds to 1 — essentially free, since it's computed during training. On the breast cancer dataset, worst radius leads at 0.133, followed closely by worst perimeter at 0.132, then worst concave points, worst area, and mean concave points. Five of thirty features carry about 60 percent of the total.

But impurity importance reflects how the trees were built, not necessarily how useful a feature is on new data. Permutation importance asks a more direct question — if I shuffle this one column in the test set, breaking its link to the target, how much does the model's score drop? A big drop means the model truly relies on it.

Here the ranking shifts — worst radius still leads, but worst area jumps to second and worst texture to third, a feature that didn't even appear in the impurity top five. Each value is the average accuracy drop across 10 shuffles, and it's computed on held-out data, a more honest measure of what matters for real generalization.

Notice the permutation values are small — shuffling even the single best feature costs only about 2 points of accuracy. That's because many of these features are near-duplicates. Worst radius and worst perimeter are correlated at 0.994, and worst area tracks them too, since all three describe the size of the same cell nucleus. Shuffle one, and the model simply leans on its siblings instead.

With correlated features, importance gets split or hidden among the whole group, and the ranking within that group is fairly arbitrary. Plotting both methods side by side makes the disagreement visible directly.

Five pitfalls to remember. Correlated features share credit, so treat a cluster as a group. Importance is not causation — a feature the model relies on isn't necessarily a lever you can pull. Importance gives no direction, only magnitude — use partial dependence plots for that. Compute it on held-out data when you can. And a suspiciously dominant feature is a red flag for data leakage.

In practice, drop near-zero importance features and recheck validation performance, sanity-check against domain knowledge, and communicate carefully — the model relies most on radius-related measurements is fair, radius causes malignancy is not. To recap: impurity importance is free and fast, permutation importance is model-agnostic and measured on held-out data, and they can disagree, especially with correlated features. That completes our tour of trees and ensembles. Next: k-nearest neighbors and Naive Bayes.
